text: That came a bit later.. But this was something else (Post-edit : KP is partially right... Watermarks already existed, but were made a lot more complex through these efforts)
This was asked here tangentially Political prisoners were used to produce them

Yup During WWII, Nazi Germany launched Operation Bernhard to produce high-quality counterfeit British pounds — replicating not only the printing, but also the special “rag-paper / watermark paper” used for genuine notes. The paper for the genuine British banknotes had been supplied by Portals (the company) — in other words, the same kind of “security paper” that legitimate banknotes used. Because the forgeries were so good — visually and by “feel,” even testing by experts initially often failed to detect them — the forgery-operation demonstrated that existing security was insufficient. As a response to these risks, after the war, banknotes were redesigned and new security features - embedded security threads, and making even more complex watermarks (@Kartikey Pradhan sorry, you were partially right)... became more standard, to make counterfeiting harder.
